I am very absentminded and clumsy and have a stainless steel sink. I have broken a french press and two Chemex's, one with which I barely grazed the faucet and chipped a tiny but obvious, perfectly round hole right in the pour spout.

My solution has been to use a collapsible silicon type of over-the-cup dripper, which was tolerable although not ideal when using the triple-layer muslin filter I made for my Chemex. However, I destroyed the filter when cleaning it (accidentally cooked all the water out of the pot I was boiling it in and burned the filter it to a crisp) and switched to paper filters. I find these inconvenient, because I have to remember to go out and buy them, and annoyingly often they split at the seam and dump coffee grounds into my cuppa. The paper taste also gets into the coffee somehow, I'm sure of it.

I developed another problem with my silicone dripper after switching to paper filters. Due to physical properties of liquids completely unbeknownst to me, the coffee, instead of dripping down to my cup, would run like a capillary across the flat part of the filter and drip OUTSIDE of my cup. This was avoided by making the coffee in a cup large enough to encompass the whole perimeter of the silicone coffee maker, but sometimes this required balancing acts using chopsticks and wooden spoons, and due to clumsiness and absentmindedness this became undesirable.

So I bought a hard plastic coffee dripper

It worked perfectly for about a month then just stopped filtering correctly. It will slowly filter about 6 out of 12 ounces then just stop up. If you tap on the side it will start filtering a little again. I thought it was the size of the coffee grind so I put the grounds in a rinsed coffee filter to see what would happen and the results were the same.

Other than it not filtering anymore I realized I hate how you have to empty this thing. You have one of three options:

1) Rinse it out and pour everything down the drain which has been known to stop up grease traps.
2) Scoop the grounds out and wipe it clean using a paper towel.
3) Then there's the way I imagine most of us use which is to tap or scoop the grinds into a trash bin and then rinse what's left out.

No matter which method you pick it's a pain in the butt to empty.
